newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS TO BE TRIED OVER SENNA DEATH.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS TO BE TRIED OVER SENNA DEATH.

text.p: Formula One team chief Frank Williams and five other people will go on trial in Italy next February charged with manslaughter over the death of Brazilian driver Ayrton Senna, Williams's Italian lawyer said on Monday.

Lawyer Roberto Causo said the first hearing had been set for February 20 before a local judge in Imola, where Senna, a Brazilian, was killed in a crash during the San Marino Grand Prix on May 1, 1994.
Causo represents Frank Williams, the Williams team technical director Patrick Head, chief designer Adrian Newey and Belgian race director Roland Bruynseraede in the case.

"We deny the charges absolutely," Causo said. He declined to say whether any of his clients would attend the trial. Under Italian law, defendants can exercise a right to stay away from proceedings against them.

Also charged with manslaughter are Imola race track director Federico Bendinelli and a former track official, Giorgio Poggi. They too deny the charges. One of their lawyers, Roberto Landi, also confirmed the February 20 hearing.
Senna, three times world champion, suffered fatal head injuries when his Williams car smashed into a wall on Imola's Tamburello curve during the race in 1994.
